findings.element: The owner's measure — .b-item, when two moments land close together or on the same day
findings.problem: Put a second moment on a day that already has one — one press of −7 on the demo plan does it — and the earlier row's Edit control stops responding to the pointer at every width I drove (390, 768, 1024, 1152, 1279, 1280, 1440). Not the wrong editor: nothing at all. The click dies silently. .b-item is position:absolute pinned to its true pixel, and --push is applied as margin-top on .b-copy, so the crowded row's own box still starts on the true pixel and grows to push + copy height while its visible content sits at the bottom of it. At 1440 the follow row's box runs 434→628 with its words at 536→628; the empty 102px on top lies exactly over the lead row's copy at 434→525, and a transparent div still hit-tests. elementsFromPoint over the lead row's Edit returns the follow .b-item first, the .b-grab second. Keyboard still works, so this is invisible to anyone tabbing and invisible to the gate, which asserts two moments can share a day and that they are grouped rather than overprinted but never that both stay pressable. The row it takes out is the worst one to take out: the lead — the next thing, the one wearing the only indigo mark. And on the flagship case this is not an edge, it is the shape of the plan: a wedding day holds ceremony, photographs, dinner and first dance on one date.
findings.fix: In b.css, beside the .b-copy rule that carries --push, add: .b-item { pointer-events: none; } and .b-item .b-copy, .b-item .b-away, .b-item .b-tick { pointer-events: auto; }. The row's transparent push band then stops hit-testing and only the drawn parts of the row take a pointer. I injected exactly this at runtime with the two moments stacked and elementsFromPoint over the lead row's Edit went from 'DIV.b-item @invitations' to 'BUTTON.b-grab @menu' at the top of the stack. Add one gate assertion beside 'two moments can share a day': after the stack forms, for every .b-grab assert document.elementFromPoint at its centre resolves inside its own .b-item.

findings.element: .b-edit in .b-editHost at every width from 1024 up
findings.problem: Press Edit at desk width and the panel opens at y=597 and runs to 1156 — 559px tall in a column that is already 925px tall because the 79-day counter sits above it. Measured on open, with no scroll: 1024x768 shows 31% of the panel, 1152x800 and 1280x800 show 36%, 1440x900 shows 54%, and 1440x960 — the width every frame in this lab was shot at — shows 65%. 'Done' sits at 1036 and 'Delete this moment' at 1100 in every one of those cases, so the primary action is between 76 and 268 pixels below the fold on open, always. At 1024x768 the only control fully on screen is the title field: the WHEN field, the four steppers and the readout — the gesture the whole product is built around — are cut off, and the owner is given no sign there is more panel. keepInBand returns early unless getComputedStyle(panel).position === 'fixed', so the sheet widths get placed and the rail widths get nothing. The behaviour gate's 'the row being edited is on screen when it opens' loop runs only at 390 and 768, which is exactly why this survived; the undo-bar-in-view check passes at 1280 and 1440 because the bar is pinned to the panel's head, the half that is on screen.
findings.fix: In openEditor(), after the panel is appended and the fixed branch has run, add an else branch for the rail: const pr = node.getBoundingClientRect(); if (pr.bottom > window.innerHeight - 24) window.scrollBy(0, Math.min(pr.top - 24, pr.bottom - window.innerHeight + 24)); — the Math.min keeps the panel's head from being pushed off while bringing its foot in. Do this on open only, not on each stepper press: round 7 refuted scrolling the measure to follow a move at desk width because it moves the steppers under a repeating hand, and that reasoning holds. Opening is not a repeat-press moment. Then extend the gate's 'the row being edited is on screen when it opens' loop to 1024x768, 1280x800 and 1440x960 and add 'the panel's primary action is on screen when it opens' asserting the [data-act=done] rect is wholly inside the viewport.

findings.problem: The whole forced-colours mapping is inert. build.mjs concatenates fonts.css, shell.css, b.css in that order, so shell.css's forced block lands at master.html line 356 and b.css's base paint lands at 491, 536, 601 and 678 — same specificity, later in the sheet, and a media query adds none. Driven with forcedColors:'active' at 1440, .b-rail computes rgba(255,255,255,0.16) rather than CanvasText, which is white at 16% on a white Canvas; .b-todayRule computes rgb(255,255,255) rather than Highlight, white on white; and the lead tick's border-color computes CanvasText rather than Highlight. The screenshot confirms it: no spine down the measure and no rule under the date. A high-contrast reader gets rows floating in space with no instrument behind them and no statement of today on the rail. Both gate assertions here pass on invisible pixels, because they only test that the value is not transparent — 'the rail is drawn in forced colours' is satisfied by 16% white on white. The one thing that does survive is the lead tick's 3px ring, which is the one thing the gate measures by geometry.
findings.fix: Move the @media (forced-colors: active) block out of shell.css and into the foot of b.css, so it is concatenated after the paint it is meant to override; nothing inside it changes. Then tighten the two gate assertions from 'not transparent' to a real comparison against the ground: assert getComputedStyle('.b-rail').backgroundColor is not equal to the composited page background, and the same for .b-todayRule, both measured after compositing alpha over the body background rather than by string inequality.

findings.element: .b-undo when the editor is closed, below 1024
findings.problem: Below 1024 the reversibility bar becomes position:fixed at bottom:12px, z-index 4 — 77px tall at 390, 54px at 768 — and nothing reserves the band it occupies. The reserve and the scroll-padding are both scoped to [data-editor-open]: the field's padding-bottom stays at 28px at 390 and 56px at 768, and scroll-padding-bottom computes 'auto' because [data-editor-open] { scroll-padding-bottom: var(--b-sheet, 30px) } does not match once the panel is closed. Driven at 390 and at 768: move a moment, press Done, scroll to the top, then Tab. The fourth Tab lands on 'Edit Venue walk-through' with the browser parking it at 800–828 against a bar top of 755 — the control has focus, is completely behind the bar, and elementFromPoint at its centre returns the bar. That is the exact sequence a phone owner performs after their most frequent action, and it produces a focused control they cannot see and cannot press. This is the one floating object in the product that does not get a reserved band, and the gate only ever checks the band under the editor sheet.
findings.fix: In the max-width:1023px block, change the two guards from [data-editor-open] to [data-editor-open], [data-undo="true"] so the reserve and the scroll padding follow the bar as well as the sheet, and set --b-undo (the bar's measured height) alongside --b-sheet: [data-editor-open], [data-undo="true"] { scroll-padding-bottom: var(--b-sheet, var(--b-undo, 90px)); } and [data-medium] .b-field[data-editor-open], [data-medium] .b-field[data-undo="true"] { padding-bottom: var(--b-sheet, var(--b-undo, 90px)); }. Write --b-undo in paintUndo() from the bar's offsetHeight + 24 whenever it fills, and clear it when the stack empties, the way openEditor already writes --b-sheet. Assert it: with the panel closed and the bar filled, Tab through every .b-grab at 390 and 768 and require elementFromPoint at each focused control's centre to resolve inside that control.

findings.element: .b-item:hover .b-copy, on both the guest surfaces and the crowded owner rows
findings.problem: The hover model is inverted at both ends. On the guest surfaces every row answers the cursor with a 12px halo — .b-copy goes from transparent to rgba(255,255,255,0.04) with a matching box-shadow on phone, desk and print, measured at 390 and 1440 — and those rows carry no control at all, no .b-grab, cursor:auto, and nothing happens when they are clicked. The audience surface, the one screen the company is judged on, promises seven openable rows and delivers none. At the other end, an owner row that IS openable stops answering the moment it crowds: .b-item[data-crowded="true"] .b-copy is declared at b.css:371 with the same (0,3,0) specificity as the .b-item:hover / :focus-within rule at 365 and later in source, so it wins outright — driven at both 390 and 1440, a crowded row's .b-copy is byte-identical at rest, on hover and on focus-within. This is the craft-plumbing lesson the library already paid for, state rules landing after interaction rules at equal specificity, back in the file it was written about.
findings.fix: Two lines. Scope the hover to rows that can actually be opened: change .b-item:hover .b-copy, .b-item:focus-within .b-copy to .b-item:has(.b-grab):hover .b-copy, .b-item:has(.b-grab):focus-within .b-copy, so a guest row is inert to the cursor as it is to the click. Then move the .b-item[data-crowded="true"] .b-copy rule ABOVE the hover and focus-within rules in b.css and give the interaction rules their tint as a custom property the crowded rule does not touch — .b-copy { background: var(--row-fill, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px var(--row-fill, transparent); }, crowded sets --row-fill: var(--back), hover and focus-within set --row-fill: var(--fore-04) — so the crowded opaque plate and the hover answer stop fighting for the same declaration. Assert that a crowded row's computed .b-copy background changes under hover.

biggestWin: The reversibility model. One history stack, one bar, and every entry carrying its own undo closure rather than a single hard-coded reversal — so a move, a rename, a hide, an add and a delete all take back the same way, and the bar physically travels into the editing panel so the offer is beside the button that filled it rather than a thousand pixels below it. What lifts it past competent is what undo restores: the entry captures window.scrollY at the moment of the change and the stepper entry carries a focus closure, so pressing Ctrl+Z after a move puts the moment back, puts the owner's view back where they were standing, and returns focus to the exact button they pressed — with preventScroll on every focus call so the place restore is not undone by the focus restore, and the restore in a finally so a throw inside a closure cannot strand it. I drove move, rename, hide, add and delete at 390, 768 and 1440 and could not find a path that lost either place or focus. Products four times this size do not get this right, and it is the piece of this artifact that is already at the Linear bar.
